paraphrase: The spotless one, the first Lord, who made me servant to his servants, the pure one, lord of the immortals, Lord of Araṅgam — his feet came and entered my eyes.
speaker: Tiruppāṇ Āḻvār
notes: 'amalaṉ ātipirāṉ aṭiyārkku eṉṉai āṭpaṭutta vimalaṉ'. Wording of the second half moderate.

paraphrase: The cloud-hued one, who as a cowherd ate the butter and stole my heart, lord of the celestials, the jewel of Araṅgam, my nectar — the eyes that have seen him will see nothing else.
speaker: Tiruppāṇ Āḻvār
notes: 'kaṇṭa kaṇkaḷ maṟṟoṉṟiṉaik kāṇāvē' — by tradition his last words before merging into the Lord.

paraphrase: The Lord's form is seen part by part as he is carried in — his feet, his red garment, his navel from which Brahmā arose, his waist, his chest where Śrī dwells, his throat that swallowed the worlds, his red mouth, his wide eyes.
speaker: Tiruppāṇ Āḻvār
notes: The feet-to-crown (pādādi-keśa) contemplation of the image of Raṅganātha.
